status_summary: The US Mission to the UN informed the Declaration's coalition by diplomatic note dated 2025-01-24 that the United States rejoins the Geneva Consensus Declaration, and on 2026-08-12 the Secretaries of Health and Human Services and of State announced that the secretariat was returning to the United States, housed in the HHS Office of Global Affairs and run jointly by HHS and State. Under that secretariat, three more countries joined on 2026-09-23, bringing the total to 46 signatories. State released scaled-back 2024 country human rights reports on 2025-08-12; related rollbacks of gender, equity and abortion-related foreign assistance and withdrawals from UN bodies are covered in c09-03, c09-04 and c06-03. No document adopting the Commission on Unalienable Rights report as policy was found.

timeline.event: The US Mission to the United Nations sent a diplomatic note (EXEC 2025-08) to the Declaration's coalition missions stating that the United States rejoins the Geneva Consensus Declaration.
timeline.source: US Mission to the UN (diplomatic note, hosted by the Institute for Women's Health)

timeline.event: State released the 2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices in a streamlined format that dropped dedicated sections on several rights, such as fair trial, privacy and freedom of movement, per CRS.

The Secretaries of State and of Health and Human Services announced in a joint statement that the Geneva Consensus Declaration secretariat returns to the United States after Hungary's stewardship, housed in the HHS Office of Global Affairs and led jointly by HHS and State.

The US-run Geneva Consensus Declaration secretariat, housed in the HHS Office of Global Affairs and operated jointly with State, reported that Honduras, Trinidad and Tobago and Algeria joined the Declaration at a side event during the UN General Assembly high-level week, bringing the total to 46 signatories.

title: Align foreign policy with the Geneva Consensus Declaration and unalienable-rights report
uncertainties: The diplomatic note was read as hosted by a private organization that led the Declaration's drafting, not on a government site; its content matches an HHS Office of Global Affairs readout of 2026-08-13 stating that the United States rejoined in January 2025, though that readout gives no day, and an HHS statement of 2025-01-27 by the Acting Secretary (hhs.gov, read on 2026-10-26) celebrates the rejoining without giving a day, so the 2025-01-24 date still rests on the hosted note. An undated Voice of America editorial page (editorials.voa.gov) attributes the rejoining announcement to the Secretary of State; it is not kept as a source because the page gives no date. The same 2026-08-13 readout dates the US assumption of the secretariat to June 2026, while the joint statement announcing it is dated 2026-08-12; the record uses the statement date. The September 2026 readout carries a 2026-09-24 page date and a 2026-09-23 New York dateline; the event uses the dateline, and the side event was hosted by a civil society coalition rather than by the government. State Department pages other than the Foreign Affairs Manual could not be read directly; searches of state.gov and usmission.gov on 2026-10-26 for the rejoin statement returned only advocacy, encyclopedia and news pages. A June 2025 Just Security analysis described a State reorganization proposal for an Office of Natural Rights within a restructured human rights bureau; as an analysis of a plan it is kept as a source, not an event. 1 FAM 510 as transmitted on 2025-03-20 (fam.state.gov) lists no Office of Natural Rights in the Bureau of Democracy, Human Rights, and Labor, but it predates the July 2025 reorganization, so whether the office was created was not confirmed. The Commission on Unalienable Rights report was not found cited in any current State document, and none of the fetched sources mention it. The CRS summary of the country reports describes the removed sections but does not link them to the Commission. Inference: implemented reflects the Declaration steps and the related rollbacks recorded elsewhere; the Commission-based structural changes the text asks for are not shown.
